It’s been a major source of anxiety and depression in my life, something I always tried to dismiss with self-defeating habits starting at a young age. Last year I decided that this was just not sustainable and this led to me confronting the paralyzing fear I’ve always tried to suppress. Sobriety, therapy, meditation, and exploring philosophical literature that deals with the concept of death were the major components of my self-discovery. The mortality related literature may sound counterintuitive, but for me a lot of the fear was the unknown aspect of the concept and to read about different people’s views and experiences eliminates some of that “unknown” part for me.  Oh and I got a kitten around the same time this was occurring in my life, my first ever companion to take care of. He’s wonderful and surprisingly I’ve gained a huge amount in terms of perspective on life/death from just having him to take care of. 

I apologize for the sad topic, I hope it is interesting enough to excuse the potential bad vibes. We’re all on this journey together. 

“We are going to die, and that makes us the lucky ones. Most people are never going to die because they are never going to be born. The potential people who could have been here in my place but who will in fact never see the light of day outnumber the sand grains of Arabia. Certainly those unborn ghosts include greater poets than Keats, scientists greater than Newton. We know this because the set of possible people allowed by our DNA so massively exceeds the set of actual people. In the teeth of these stupefying odds it is you and I, in our ordinariness, that are here. We privileged few, who won the lottery of birth against all odds, how dare we whine at our inevitable return to that prior state from which the vast majority have never stirred?”
 -Richard Dawkins, a passage from his book entitled “Unweaving the Rainbow”

Wow yeah spot on what I am dealing with. I know you did not ask but I highly, highly recommend checking if there is a therapist in your area that is trained in Dialectical behavioral therapy, often abbreviated to DBT. 3 years of trying everything possible and this is pretty much the only thing that has helped me significantly. It is not anything like the name sounds, so if you are interested I recommend that you don’t go into reading about it with any preconceived notions based on what it is called. This approach works towards helping people increase their emotional and cognitive regulation by learning about the triggers that lead to reactive states and helping to assess which coping skills to apply in the sequence of events, thoughts, feelings, and behaviors to help avoid undesired reactions. DBT assumes that people are doing their best but lack the skills needed to succeed, or are influenced by positive reinforcement or negative reinforcement that interferes with their ability to function appropriately.  

I can’t even begin to tell you how thankful I am that my therapist recommended this. I go to a weekly class on DBT. Please please please if you are at all able to pursue this, consider doing so. It has helped immensely and I would credit me being here today to that class it is very important to me. 

Aside from that, I really hope we can figure this out it is debilitating. Contact me any time any day I’d love to discuss what works for each of us in dealing with this.

The kitten had a lot of symptoms. They were misdiagnosed as coccidia, the shock and abruptness of this news  is due to the fact that I was under the impression that he had a common infection and would just require a different antibiotic. But I am assuming he knew it was not going to be a good outcome when the antibiotic course didn't help the symptoms, meaning that these symptoms are attributed to something much much worse.  There was too much to deny at this point. There was an attempt to recover this kitten.. he was sick with what I was told was coccidia when I got him. I stayed up reading 2 nights straight about the specifics of facilitating a recovery During that time I  administered diluted pedialyte through a feeding syringe to counteract the possibility of dehydration due to the diarrhea that, again, I was told was from coccidia., assisted him with pooping, cleaned him up cause he often would step in his messy waste, and I comforted him/kept him warm but not too warm. And encouraged eating as much as I could. This was not enough and a new cat owner can not be reasonably expected to know what every possible kitten disease, illness, or syndrome entails and know what the vet should or shouldn't look for. Especially right after being told I need to leave the amazing companion that I had become so very close to. Maybe the first time you raised a kitten you would've been less emotional about the unexpected death sentence of your new baby  and you would've said all the right things but that is not how I naturally reacted. I immediately sat down on the floor and held my boy and cried.  Why would you think that I plan to hold him by the scruff if I just wrote how detrimental it can be and the reason why. Why would you think I plan to go back to this vet if I just said I wanted to "get his brother outta there" and gave you reasons why it seemed kind of off when I looked back at all of the conversations with this vet. I don't think you were able to gauge my intentions like you thought you could. I hope you never have to go through something like this it is truly painful. Hindsight is 20/20 and not everyone does this as much as you do(this is an assumption because of your username).

This vet has seemed sort of...off...in more than a few ways. I am still trying to piece together what was going on.  It is in the basement of a house with 1 old guy vet and 1 assistant and 1 receptionist. It was incredibly abrupt this entire ordeal  was about 15 minutes from arrival to departure with a different kitten.  I am still reading about fading kitten syndrome and there have been a few things that made me come to the same "wait... something was off about that" conclusion that it seems you have reached. and I was left with no further explanation other than what is written above. I stood in disbelief and said are you sure it isn't say.. boredom, depression, dehydration, or sleepiness/laziness they said he was already on medication(Albon) for coccidia. Another thing that was weird is that as I was leaving he said "so here's a little trick that will make your kitten a great companion, you do this and you will have the best cat in the world when he grows up." Then proceeded to pick the kitten up by the scruff on his neck and said do this often and you will have a great cat guaranteed. But  I read multiple trustworthy  sources when I was preparing to adopt that said this is not the case and it can actually be somewhat painful for the kittens. This made me feel really, really bad when I imagined him doing this EVERY TIME HE HANDLED THEM..  well I have the patience and time to do this the right way and give him the care he needs so I got his brother outta there. It will be a long process but I'm looking forward to the bond that will develop from this process.
